technical_body.purpose: Primary craft interface for the 5ESS. Reached via TTY on the SM (Switching Module) or via maintenance modem on the 5ESS's dial-up DID. Menu tree with numeric addressing.

load_verify_pattern.notes: Any change that has not been executed still leaves an audit trail entry in the RC log.

technical_body.purpose: View / modify subscriber-line class-of-service and feature membership.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Set a target line's FGD trunk permissions, lift toll restrictions, or add IN (Intelligent Network) features. Also the entry point for adjusting a line's screening class (see 12.1).

technical_body.purpose: View / modify trunk-group configuration: FGD, FGB, WATS, DID, tie-lines. Set outgoing signaling type (MF R1, ISUP, PRI).
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Manipulate what signaling a specific trunk group speaks — e.g., configure an outbound MF R1 trunk group for legacy tandem behavior.

technical_body.purpose: Query the switch's translation database. Look up how a specific number is currently routed.
Add or modify call-forwarding features on a subscriber line: variable CF, remote-access CF, busy-line CF, don't-answer CF.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Adding a call-forward pointing at a target number gives you a diverter — a subscribed line becomes a free relay to wherever you point it.

technical_body.purpose: Add / modify CLASS custom-calling features: caller ID, call waiting, three-way calling, speed calling, distinctive ringing, anonymous call rejection.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Toggle CLASS features on a target line without their consent — enable / disable caller ID delivery, block anonymous rejection to defeat *67 blocking.

technical_body.purpose: Line-class screening: which NPA codes / prefixes a line may dial, toll restrictions, 900/976 blocking.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Lift a target line's toll restrictions (or add them to a hostile line). Bypass 900/976 blocking without the subscriber knowing.

technical_body.purpose: Live-callable command from RCV. Enables real-time call-trace logging on a target DN.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Hostile from an attacker's viewpoint. Any 5ESS an attacker is touching is capable of logging their session in real time via TRACE, and cover-your-tracks requires knowing whether TRACE is active on your own DN before you begin.

technical_body.notes: These were documented in Phrack 33 and 52, and were widely rotated after ~1995. Any modern 5ESS deployment will have replaced them; era-authentic CTF scenarios reproduce them faithfully.

technical_body.purpose: Maintenance and Administration Position Command Interpreter. The DMS family's craft interface — reached via TTY on the IOC (I/O Controller) or via maintenance modem.
top_level_command_hierarchy: TABLE — direct table access (OFCVAR, OFCENG, OFCOPT, OFCSTD, CLLI, TRKGRP, LENLINES)
technical_body.backchannel_note: DMS switches in Canada were historically reachable via NT's private X.25 'Datapac' back-network — a common era-authentic entry point for phreaks.

technical_body.purpose: Add / change / remove subscriber lines. Analogous to Meridian PBX LD 10/11 but for CO subscribers.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Add a new subscriber line for yourself on the DMS, or CHF a target line's features / class of service.

technical_body.purpose: Direct access to internal translation tables — the raw provisioning database.

key_tables.CLLI: Common Language Location Identifier — the office's own CLLI code + all reachable-office CLLIs
key_tables.LENLINES: line equipment number to DN mapping

technical_body.phreak_relevance: Dump CLLI reachability with `TABLE CLLI; POS 0; NEXT` (etc.). Read OFCVAR to learn the office's carrier-partition constants — critical for understanding what dial-plan tricks are possible on this switch.

technical_body.purpose: Line Test Position. Seize a subscriber line, hang them up, apply milliwatt / balance test / ring the line.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: Test-position access to any subscriber loop. On old generics, this included MONITOR — bridge into an active call. Bell-lawful use case: repair-craft testing; phreak use case: silent line monitoring.

technical_body.purpose: Trunk Test Position. Seize a specific trunk member and put it in various test states: SEIZE, MB (make busy), BSY (busy-out), RTS (return to service), MONITOR.
technical_body.phreak_relevance: MONITOR seizes a trunk and puts you in the audio path of the current call. On old DMS generics with `permit CI TTP MONITOR` enabled, this was a wiretap. Later generics required a warrant + separate CALEA path.

technical_body.purpose: System log utility — the DMS's log buffer of switch events (subscriber activations, alarms, craft commands run, TRACE hits).
technical_body.phreak_relevance: The thing to disable if you're covering tracks. `LOGUTIL; STOPDEV <log-device>` suppresses log output to a specific device. Analogous to Meridian PBX LD 40 CDR suppression.

name: DMS MAPCI — era-typical default craft logins

technical_body.notes: Documented in vendor training and Phrack 5.5 (Knight Lightning). Widely rotated after ~1995. Bell operating companies rotated first; independent telcos and PTT/incumbent operators in some countries kept defaults longer.
